description: Mido and the forest exit stop blocking Link, as child or adult
label: Open Forest

description: The Kakariko gate guard has already seen Zelda's letter, so the Death Mountain trail is open from the start
label: Open Kakariko Gate

description: Link starts having met Zelda, with her letter in hand, and Talon and Malon back at Lon Lon Ranch. Her letter's check holds the letter. Impa's check comes at the start (Zelda's Lullaby, unless Songs are shuffled), and Malon's does too when NPC gifts are shuffled. Zelda's Letter and the Weird Egg have been removed from the pool
label: Met Zelda

description: With Open, the Door of Time stands open from the start, so Link can grow up without the stones or the Song of Time. Zelda and Impa stay until he's met them. He skips Rauru, whose gift comes at the start, and can put the sword back any time. With Closed, it opens as in the game: once Link has met Zelda, brought the three stones to her scene at the moat, and plays the Song of Time on the Ocarina of Time
label: Door of Time

description: Jabu-Jabu's mouth is open, so child Link walks in without giving him a fish
label: Jabu-Jabu Open

description: The waterfall at the end of Zora's River already stands split, so Link reaches Zora's Domain without Zelda's Lullaby
label: Zora's River Waterfall Open

description: The debris in front of the Deku Tree's mouth is gone, so adult Link walks in and out
label: Adult Deku Tree

description: How the four carpenters in the Gerudo Fortress start. With Normal, Link frees all four, as in the game. With Fast, freeing any one frees all four and earns the membership card, and the other thieves still guard their cells. With Freed, all four are free from the start, with the membership card in hand, the guards standing down and the valley bridge up. Their thieves still stand, and beating one opens her cell without freeing anyone twice
label: Gerudo Fortress

description: What people hand over becomes a check: their gifts, minigame prizes, the House of Skulltula's rewards and the Great Fairies' upgrades
label: NPC Gifts

description: Twelve songs become checks, given without the lesson: Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Saria's Song, the Sun's Song, the Song of Time, the Song of Storms and Sheik's six. The Scarecrow's Song stays where it is
label: Songs

description: With NPC gifts on, the House of Skulltula's reward for all 100 tokens is a check too. Off, it pays its Gold Rupee as always, and logic never sends Link for all 100
label: 100-Token Reward

description: Each trade on the way to Biggoron's sword becomes a check, from Anju's Pocket Egg to Biggoron's Claim Check, and the ten trade items join the pool. Showing an item to the one who wants it gives that check, whatever order Link finds them in. Grog or Fado waits at the stump by which item Link holds. The Pocket Cucco still hatches from the egg
label: Adult Trade Quest

description: People who sell one thing sell a check once, for the price of the thing: Medigoron's Giant's Knife, the carpet merchant's Bombchus, and the bean seller's first bean. Bombchus and beans stay on sale after that
label: Merchants

description: The pedestal holds an item from the pool, and the Master Sword can turn up anywhere. Pulling or returning the sword still travels through time without it. Adult Link without it has no sword
label: Master Sword

description: Shelf slots in the eight shops sell checks, each once, at a random price. Prices over 99 rupees need a bigger wallet in logic
label: Shopsanity

description: How many slots of each shop sell a check with Shopsanity on. The rest sell what they always did
label: Shop Slots

description: The fourteen heart pieces lying out in the world are checks. One that holds something else shows it, spinning where the piece was
label: Freestanding Heart Pieces

description: Each of the eight cows gives a check once, for Epona's Song. After that it gives milk, which still needs a bottle
label: Cows

description: Each of the 100 Gold Skulltulas drops a check when killed. A token for each goes in the pool, so the House of Skulltula still counts them. Logic wants the Boomerang or Hookshot for every one
label: Gold Skulltulas

description: The heart container each of the eight bosses leaves behind is a check
label: Boss Heart Containers

description: The Spiritual Stones and five medallions become checks, given by the scene after each boss. Light stays with Rauru
label: Dungeon Rewards

description: Each dungeon's map and compass turn up at random checks anywhere, and mark their own dungeon wherever Link finds them. Keys stay where they are
label: Maps and Compasses

description: With Start, Link holds every dungeon's small keys and boss key from the start. The 43 chests that held a key become checks. With Start each brings a Red Rupee to the pool. The two keys lying in the open stay where they are
label: Keys

description: With Start, Link holds the four Gerudo Fortress keys from the start, so every cell opens whatever the thieves drop. With Keysanity, each key turns up at a random check, anywhere. Either way, the four keys the thieves carry become checks
label: Fortress Keys

description: What caps the Bombchus Link holds. The bomb bag's, as in the game. Their own cap of 40, so they open the same checks bombs do without waiting on the bag. Or three Bombchu Bags in the pool, holding 20, 30 and 40, and none until the first
label: Bombchus

description: Turns on every skip below. Cutscenes that give an item, set a flag or move Link still play
label: Skip All Cutscenes

description: All small makes every chest a small one, which opens without the big chest's long animation. What a chest holds doesn't change
label: Chest Size

description: Navi never stops Link to talk on her own: the Lost Woods warning, dungeon and quest tips, and reminders. Hints you ask her for still work
label: Quiet Navi

description: Link runs half again as fast while he wears the Bunny Hood
label: Bunny Hood Speed

description: Every Business Scrub outside the Dream World sells a check once. Scrubs that sold ammo on repeat sell their one item and leave
label: Business Scrubs

description: The running man's prize for Link's first win becomes a check. Later wins still pay a Red Rupee. Logic expects it only with Gerudo Fortress Freed, since he offers the race once the valley bridge is fixed
label: Running Man's Race

description: Each pot is a check, flying pots included. One placed with no drop of its own brings a Recovery Heart, a Deku Stick and the like to the pool. Its item stays until Link picks it up. After that the pot drops what it always did
label: Pots

description: Each wooden crate is a check. Link breaks a big one by rolling into it
label: Crates

description: Each small rock is a check. Link lifts and throws one to break it
label: Rocks

description: Each grass shrub Link can cut or lift is a check, like those outside Saria's house
label: Grass

description: Each of Kakariko's beehives is a check. Anything thrown or shot but a slingshot seed knocks one down
label: Beehives

description: Every rupee and Recovery Heart lying loose in the world is a check, and so are the Deku Nut, Seed and Stick on Lake Hylia's bed. Each is taken once, as in the game. One that holds something else shows it where the rupee or heart was
label: Loose Items

description: The eight masks are items in the pool, less any Link starts with, and the Happy Mask Shop lends none. Off, the shop lends them in order, as in the game
label: Shuffle Masks

description: Swaps junk (rupees, ammo, recovery hearts) for ice traps. Each looks like an item logic needs until Link gets it, then says FOOL! and freezes him
label: Ice Traps

description: Upgrade chests and gifts give the next level Link doesn't have: Hookshot then Longshot, the Goron Bracelet then Silver and Gold Gauntlets, Silver then Gold Scale, Fairy Ocarina then Time, and each bag, quiver and wallet up a size
label: Progressive Items

description: The Small Nut Bag is an item in the pool, and Link holds no Deku Nuts until he finds it. Off, the first nut he picks up brings it, as in the game
label: Shuffle the Nut Bag

description: The Small Stick Bag is an item in the pool, and Link holds no Deku Sticks until he finds it. Off, the first stick he picks up brings it, as in the game
label: Shuffle the Stick Bag

description: The first spell, magic arrow, Lens of Truth or Improved Spin Link finds turns the magic meter on, as in the game. Off, only a Magic Meter or Doubled Magic does, and a Magic Meter joins the pool
label: Magic Comes with the First Magic Item

description: Glitchless places each item where Link can reach it without that item, so a seed can always be beaten. No logic places items anywhere, so a seed may not be
label: Logic

description: How old Link is on a new file. Adult wakes in the Temple of Time, and opens the Door of Time and the forest, so he can go back to child and walk out. He holds the Master Sword only when the start inventory does: otherwise the pedestal gives its check on his first pull back to adult.
label: Starting Age

description: What raises the bridge to Ganon's Castle. With Vanilla, Link walks onto the ledge once Zelda has given him the Light Arrows, as in the game. With Six Medallions, it rises once he holds all six, without the Light Arrows first. With Open, the bridge stands from the start
label: Rainbow Bridge

description: With All Six, the barrier to Ganon's tower comes down once Link clears the castle's six trials, as in the game. With Done, all six barriers are down from the start
label: Ganon's Trials

description: King Zora has read Ruto's letter and stands aside for child Link, as he does once he's shown it. Ruto's Letter becomes an empty bottle, shuffled from its spot at the bottom of the lake
label: King Zora Moved

description: Jabu-Jabu waits in the frozen fountain for adult Link too, from the start or once the Water sage is done. Adult Link walks in when his mouth is open (the Jabu-Jabu open preset), but only child Link's Boomerang beats the tentacles and Barinade. With dungeon entrances shuffled, his door leads wherever it leads for child Link
label: Adult Jabu-Jabu

description: Gold Skulltulas that only come out at night show at any hour
label: Gold Skulltulas by Day

description: What every Business Scrub asks for its check, with Business scrubs on
label: Scrub Price

description: Enemies never show, so nothing grabs Link or knocks him back. Gold Skulltulas, scrubs, Big Poes, the Skull Kid and enemies that are checks stay. For the play harness's seeds
label: Quiet Enemies

description: Menu pages skip their guide pop-up the first time they fill, and the challenge tapestry is open from the start, without the reveal it plays the first time it opens
label: Menus Open

description: Time passes from the start, as it does once Link first walks into Hyrule Field. Off, the clock waits for the field, even in a seed that starts past it
label: Clock Runs

description: Every guide screen counts as already shown, so none pops up the first time, such as the Echo Gem's in the House of Skulltula. The Great Fairy's guide still shows
label: No Tutorials

description: Recovery hearts, fairies, rupees, magic jars, arrows and Deku seeds count as picked up before, so the first one doesn't stop Link with its get text
label: No Pickup Texts

description: Each gossip stone names where an item Link needs is hidden, without the Mask of Truth or any small talk
label: Gossip Stone Hints

description: Each cutscene skipped, with Skip Cutscenes off. On, it skips them all
label: Skipped Cutscenes

options.label: Skip Meeting the Great Deku Tree

description: Each item either Link can use: child Link the adult's, adult Link the child's
label: Both Ages
